rv.q: Richard Jones's revival of Samuel Beckett's play is inspired.
Richard Jones's rigorously clear production nicely balances comic absurdity with despair.
Jones breathes new life into a play at risk of choking on its own aspic.
Beckett adds some knockabout moments but the piece is bottom-of-the-drawer fare...Cumming creates the illusion that it is weightier than it is.'
This mostly dire evening needs it.
This production has many good points, and proves what we have known for a while: that modernism is not longer obscure.

cn.t: Mixed reviews for this Beckett revival: critics praise Radcliffe and Cumming's comedic timing and chemistry, though some find the material itself thin despite the stars' efforts to elevate it.
